decisive_items: violaceous pretibial lesions with areas of necrosis
pretibial lesions of violaceous coloration, similar to retiform purpura, below the knee, associated with a necrotic lesion in the right calf
response.rationale: CKD stage 3 with diabetes and intensely painful retiform purpura/necrosis despite palpable pedal pulse strongly favors calciphylaxis. HIT is less likely because platelet count is normal (173×10⁹/L) and there is no lesion at the heparin injection site; APS is contradicted by negative autoimmunity; warfarin-induced necrosis lacks warfarin exposure.

rejected.why: No warfarin was administered; only subcutaneous heparin is mentioned.
Autoimmunity studies were negative, lacking APS-specific antibody support.
Platelet count is not thrombocytopenic and lesions are not at the heparin injection site; positive antiplatelet antibody alone is insufficient.
Same condition as R2 but misspelled and without the renal-risk-factor evidence; R2 is the better-supported calciphylaxis candidate.
